Across [[t:Hull]], the model is most sensitive to an area's own data — that is, shows the highest [[t:GeoSensitivity]] — in [[t:Old Town]] ([[n:22.33]], Kingston upon Hull 029E), with other high-sensitivity areas in Dairycoates and Sculcoates. The lowest values are found in [[t:Gipsyville]] ([[n:-1.33]]), East Ella, and Bilton Grange. Overall, GeoSensitivity is in the upper tail for these high-ranked LSOAs. [[t:Spatial clustering]] is present: [[n:9]] LSOAs are classed High–High, forming a contiguous pattern (Moran's I [[n:0.22]], p = [[n:0.001]]; pattern scale is not established). 142 LSOAs show no significant local clustering. These results describe sensitivity to area data, not crime counts or location features.

Citywide, the model relies most on [[t:crime history features]] ([[n:61%]] of total attribution), followed by census population variables ([[n:20%]]) and [[t:built environment features]] ([[n:14%]]). Within the built-environment share, [[t:retail]] ([[n:2.7%]]) and [[t:green space]] ([[n:2.6%]]) lead overall. The areas where the model relies most heavily on built-environment features are Longhill ([[n:45%]], led by green space), Avenues (green space), Bilton Grange (intersections), Sculcoates (green space), and Orchard Park (transit stops). In contrast, the Old Town’s built-environment share is low at [[n:6%]], ranked 158th, with retail as its main built feature.

The dashboard highlights Kingston upon Hull 029E ([[t:Old Town]], rank 1, [[n:22.33]]) as the most geo-sensitive LSOA (local explanation dominated by [[t:crime history]], built-environment share [[n:6%]], led by retail), compared with a low-sensitivity LSOA (003C, [[n:-1.09]]). These attribution shares describe model reliance, not planning targets or causes.
